tested:
"titanium-final-*" image folder format (Nexus 9000v internal codename) - same profile.
ROOT CAUSE (2026-07-12): get_profile("titanium-final") matched no PROFILES key,
fell back to GENERIC_KVM_PROFILE with no min_ram_mb, so the QEMU provider never
bumped RAM past the generic 512 MB default. NX-OS self-checks available DRAM at
boot and reboots in an infinite loop ("This Supervisor does not have sufficient
DRAM to function") when under its ~6 GB floor - confirmed via live serial-console
probe (repeated identical crash-restart every ~15s, never reached a prompt).
ROOT CAUSE #2 (2026-07-18): "machine": "q35" and "disk_bus": "sata" here were both
wrong for Titanium - copy-pasted from the cisco-nxosv9k entry just above (which
genuinely needs q35+SATA+UEFI). Per docs/platform/node-emulation.md's own spec,
Titanium is the OLDER product and needs the legacy `pc` (i440fx) machine + virtio
disk, not q35+SATA - unlike NX-OSv 9000, it predates AHCI/UEFI support entirely.
Confirmed live 2026-07-18 with the real image (titanium-final-7.3.0.D1.1): under
q35, the kernel boots the kickstart fine ("Image verification OK") but then prints
"Unknown boot option `ide_generic.probe_mask=0x0': ignoring" followed by "No disk
detected" / "There is a problem with the compact flash. It could not be
initialized." and drops to a permanent switch(boot)# recovery shell (a reload just
repeats the same failure - confirmed the disk never actually becomes writable, not
a one-off first-boot format). This reproduced byte-identically whether the disk was
attached as virtio OR sata (ruling out disk_bus as the cause) - only switching the
*machine type* to `pc` (i440fx) fixed it: the guest's IDE_GENERIC-era kernel needs
i440fx's legacy PCI/ISA topology to enumerate its own disk at all, and q35 has no
legacy IDE controller. Re-probe with machine=pc: "No disk detected" never appears,
boot proceeds through NX-OS module bring-up straight to "User Access
Verification / login:". disk_bus reverted to virtio to match: it was never
consulted by the real disk-attach path (shared/image_profiles.disk_bus_for(),
which already defaults unmatched vendors incl. titanium to virtio, matching this
image's actual virtioa.qcow2 file) - this field only feeds the UI's displayed
hardware-defaults recommendation, but leaving it as "sata" there was a live footgun:
a user who edited a Titanium node's disk bus in the Inspector (which seeds its
dropdown from this field) and saved would write config.disk_bus="sata", which DOES
override the runtime default and reproduce the exact same lockup for real users
from the UI.
